11.40pm It was a must-win match for both teams, and one of them now heads home. 
Chasing a total as massive as 229 in such a contest means there's pressure from ball 
one, not least when you have the class and accuracy of Jasprit Bumrah in the 
opposition. Some young GT fans are seen with tears in their eyes - that's how much it 
matters. At one stage, GT needed another 81 runs from 42 balls, and had as many as 
eight wickets standing. That is when Bumrah arrived, and reminded the world of his 
superpowers. That four-run over not only changed the game, but also swung the 
Eliminator around big time. As a result, MI will play PBKS in Qualifier 2, another 
knockout match ahead of the final. 
Shubman Gill: "Last three or four overs didn't go our way, but still a very good game of 
cricket. Not easy when we drop three sitters, especially in the powerplay. Not easy for 
the bowlers to control. The message was simple: just play the game you want to play. 
The goal was the same for both [Sai Sudharsan and Washington]... Lot of positives for 
us. Last two or three games didn't go our way, but credit to all the players - especially 
Sai; he was terrific. I think 210 was par on this pitch." 
Deepak M: "Heartbreak for Sai Sudharsan" 
Ashwani Kumar: "The chat was around bowling well. The wicket was flat, and we 
wanted to stick to the plan. I wasn't sure that I would be used as Impact Sub; perhaps 
the idea first was to use a spinner. I just spoke to the coaches regarding the plan. In the 
last three balls, I just didn't want to bowl a no-ball." 
Time for the presentations 
Hardik Pandya: "At one point of time, the game was even-stevens. I thought the wicket 
got better in the second innings. The way Jonny started, for him to make our debut for 
us... the way Ro batted. He took his time. When you see important games, all these 
margins help. Its very simple: whenever you feel the game is going far [away], just get 
him. It's like Mumbai housing prices - he's that expensive! I just need to throw the ball. I 
just thought if we can keep some extra runs at the end. It was important Jassi comes 
and bowls that over, and the margin becomes bigger. It's going to be very important to 
recover well." 
Rohit Sharma is the Player of the Match: "I've got only four fifties; I think I would have 
liked to get more. I do understand the importance of playing the Eliminator. Again, a 
complete team performance. When I play, it's trying to understand how I can play my 
best. Today, after having those luck going my way, I knew I had to make the most of it. 
I'm glad I could do that, and get the team into a good position. We knew it would be 
slightly challenging with the dew coming in. I've played all those shots in the game 
before, and unfortunately, I found fielders [today]. I got lucky; those catches got 
dropped. Even after the drop, you've got to play well. It was a good bowling effort as 
well. I've watched Bairstow over the years being on the other side... we know what he 
can do upfront with the bat. Took his chances, and it came off. We always look for that 
start." 
One more game ticked off, and we're left with only two more this season. RCB are 
waiting in the final, but before that, MI and PBKS will meet in Ahmedabad on June 1. 
Tonight, MI capitalised on a flat pitch and their luck, and their total of 228 in an 
Eliminator meant GT had to go big from ball one. Sai Sudharsan again looked in great 
touch - he hit a quick 80 - but didn't get enough support from the other end. So GT's 
campaign ends, but don't forget, the action in IPL 2025 will continue. So until next time, 
this is goodnight and goodbye!
